newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks further adrift on Q1 earnings woes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks further adrift on Q1 earnings woes.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued to drift downwards in early afternoon trade Monday due to what traders said was disappointment over the recent crop of first quarter earnings.
"Company earnings have, apart from a couple of exceptions, not been very good. That's why we are down and ADRs are down, while the Dow (Jones) is up," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was down 23.85 points, or 0.63 percent, at 3,758.77.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 28.50 points at 6,767.37.
"They're down on earnings reports, that's basically it," a desk trader meanwhile said. "Kimber's earnings, for instance were a disappoinment," he added.
Kimberly Clark de Mexico (Kimber), in which Kimberly Clark Corp has a minority stake, was down 65 centavos to 29.95 pesos. The company reported earnings shortly after midsession.
Trading volume was moderate at 69.3 million shares, but traders said dealing was very slow because two cross trades alone accounted for 45 million of that total.
